title: Kaabu Empire at its height
description: Mande-speaking rulers of the Gabu region, long a western federation within Mali's orbit, become effectively independent as Mali declines.

title: Death of Nuno Tristão
place: Rio Grande estuary, off the Bissagos
description: The Portuguese caravel captain, first European to reach these coasts, is killed with most of his crew by islanders' poisoned arrows.

title: Fall of Kansala
description: A Fula army of the Imamate of Futa Jallon storms the Kaabu capital; the endangered Mande ruling families blow up their own powder magazine, ending Kaabu rule.

title: Separate colony from Cape Verde
description: Portugal appoints a separate governor for the mainland territory, detached from administration by Cape Verde.

title: Bissau becomes the capital
description: The colonial capital moves from the island town of Bolama to the mainland port of Bissau after decades of resisted occupation.

title: PAIGC founded
description: Amílcar Cabral and five others secretly found the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde.

title: Pidjiguiti massacre
description: Police fire on striking dockworkers at the Pidjiguiti quay, killing dozens; the PAIGC answers by choosing open revolt.

title: War of independence begins
description: PAIGC guerrillas attack the Portuguese garrison at Tite in the south, opening one of Africa's hardest-fought liberation wars.

title: Amílcar Cabral assassinated
description: Dissident party men seize and kill the revolutionary leader at his headquarters, eight months before independence.

title: Independence declared
description: The state of Guinea-Bissau is proclaimed unilaterally in the liberated south; most of the world recognises it before Portugal does.

title: Portugal recognises independence
description: After the April revolution in Lisbon, Portugal formally recognises the republic, with Luís Cabral as its first president.

title: Vieira overthrows Cabral
description: Prime minister João Bernardo Vieira deposes President Luís Cabral, ending the project of union with Cape Verde.

title: First multiparty elections
description: Vieira wins the presidency in the second round, in the first elections since independence with real competition.

title: Civil war
description: A revolt by the sacked army chief Ansumane Mané draws in Senegalese and Guinean troops and devastates the capital before Vieira is overthrown.

title: Ialá overthrown
description: The army deposes President Kumba Ialá, who had dissolved parliament and ruled erratically for three years.

title: Vieira returns as president
description: João Bernardo Vieira wins a disputed run-off and takes office again six years after his overthrow.

title: Vieira assassinated
description: Hours after a bomb kills the army chief, soldiers kill President Vieira in his residence.

title: Coup interrupts the election
description: The army seizes power between the rounds of the presidential election and detains the frontrunner, prolonging the cycle of coups.

title: José Mário Vaz elected
description: Elections broadly accepted as free restore constitutional rule after two years of transition.

title: Embaló elected president
description: Umaro Sissoco Embaló wins the run-off; the result is contested and recognition drags on abroad.
